title: Declan's household €6,500 sums the same sole-trader business twice (€3,500 primary + €3,000 'DM Plumbing' net)
evidence:
+    insight: "The overall risk level is assessed as medium. Declan Murphy is a self-employed plumber with six years of trading and a guarantor parent backing the application, but the income position rests on documents that are only partially on file.\n\nThe household picture is solid: the stated primary income of €3,500 and the declared €3,000 average monthly net from DM Plumbing give a household figure of €6,500, which covers the €2,450 rent at 38%.
...
+      GetIncomeSourcesByApplicationRow(
+        id: "inc-declan-1",
+        source_type: "self_employed",
+        amount_cents: 300_000,
+        note: "Average monthly net from DM Plumbing",
+      ),
...
     job_title: Some("Plumber (self-employed)"),
detail: The applicant is a self-employed plumber with no employer, so the €3,500 primary income is DM Plumbing itself; adding its €3,000 'average net' as a second component double-counts one business.
recommended_fix: Present the €3,000 as corroboration of (or discrepancy against) the stated €3,500, or attribute the additional income to a genuinely separate source.

title: Document-count convention contradicts itself between Liam's and Sara's reports
evidence:
+          "One document on file — payslips — with the landlord reference as the only other attachment. The form is the thinnest in the demo universe on corroboration.",
...
+          "Two documents on file — payslips and landlord reference. The form is otherwise fully populated, including a personal statement; bank statements are the remaining gap.",
...
+          "The current room tenancy at Ballybough Road has a landlord reference from Karen Whitmore. No evictions, gaps or arrears are declared.",
detail: Sara's report counts payslips plus landlord reference as two documents; Liam's counts payslips alone as one while his report also cites a provided Karen Whitmore landlord reference. Same data shape, two conventions.
recommended_fix: Apply one convention: either Liam has two documents on file (payslips + landlord reference) or drop the 'only other attachment' wording.

title: docs_processed assertion is circular — the test feeds and asserts the same computed value
evidence:
+fn extras_for(app_id: String) -> ExtrasShape {
+  let docs = list.length(pdf_prebake.documents_for(app_id))
+  let raw = pdf_report_data.extras_for(app_id, docs)
...
+    extras.docs_processed
+    |> should.equal(list.length(pdf_prebake.documents_for(app_id)))
detail: The test feeds list.length(documents_for(app_id)) into extras_for, then asserts the output equals list.length(documents_for(app_id)); it can only catch a dropped parameter, never a wrong document list.
recommended_fix: Pin literal expected document counts per applicant (e.g. a-aoife → 4, a-liam → 1) so documents_for regressions fail the test.
